parcel.note: CONFIRMED BY FETCH. This is the Wisconsin Department of Administration Statewide Parcel Map Database, served through the DNR: 48 fields, maxRecordCount 1000, NO TOKEN, statewide and uniform across all 72 counties. Two county-filtered queries returned data - CONAME='RACINE' gave {"count":84282} and a CONAME='OZAUKEE' attribute query returned live rows. THE DECISIVE WEAKNESS, STATED PLAINLY: THERE IS NO USE-CODE DESCRIPTION FIELD. PROPCLASS returns bare numerals and, worse, MULTI-VALUED comma-separated strings - the actual values returned were '4,5', '4,5', '1,4', '1,5', '5' - so a single parcel can carry several classes at once and any classifier must split on commas. The codes are defined in statute (Wis. Stat. 70.32(2)(a), classes 1-7) and in the Wisconsin Property Assessment Manual, so a published code manual DOES exist, but nothing in the payload is self-documenting. Also absent: year built, living area and unit count, and Wisconsin exposes no sale price in this layer. If per-building detail is needed, individual county services (Milwaukee, Waukesha, Racine) would have to be integrated separately; they were not tested.

The Lafayette Parish Assessor's own service (https://webgis.lafayetteassessor.com/arcgis/rest/services/Sidwell/TaxParcelPublic/MapServer/0, 117,864 records: AccountNumber, OwnerName, PropertyAddress, AssessedValue, StatedArea) could NOT be queried from this session - every request was blocked at the robots.txt stage - so it is NOT reported as a working endpoint. A third-party LEDA copy (services5.arcgis.com/riEeMHAEYSsj4tFW/.../2023_Parcels_Lafayette_Parish) was queried and rejected: its PrimaryUse field holds 62 opaque codes (RA, RDFM, RSLC, REK, ...) with no published key.

ranking: Ranked on (a) verified announced DIRECT jobs, (b) genuine multifamily-rental relevance - job scale relative to metro population and current permit supply, weighted down where the anchor project is badly delayed or the market is already over-supplied - and (c) whether a free machine-readable parcel/assessment endpoint was actually fetched and confirmed. RECOMMENDED FIVE: (1) PHOENIX - 17,000 verified direct jobs across four separate anchors and $292.5B of capital, the deepest and most diversified pipeline of any metro here; Maricopa's Assessor MapServer is confirmed, rich and includes sale price; the only weakness is no unit-count field, and Pinal County (the LG site) has no county API. (2) COLUMBUS - 7,000 verified direct jobs, and uniquely BOTH relevant counties are confirmed with full CAMA schemas (Franklin 163 fields, Licking 80+ with EpinCount and three generations of sale history); permit supply of 13,145 against 2.24M people is thin, which is the multifamily thesis; discounted only because Intel's fab has slipped to 2030-31. (4) SYRACUSE - 9,000 direct Micron jobs into a 652,000-person metro with flat-to-declining population and almost no recent supply is the sharpest housing-shortage setup here, and the NYS statewide parcels service is the single richest endpoint found (PROP_CLASS, FULL_MARKET_VAL, YR_BLT, SQFT_LIVING, ACRES, statewide, no token); discounted for schedule risk - groundbreaking only happened in Jan 2026 and first fab is 2030. (5) RENO - smallest absolute jobs number of the five at 3,000, but it earns its place on supply and data: only 3,180 units permitted in twelve months for 578,000 people, and Washoe County's nightly Assessor feed is the ONLY confirmed endpoint in the entire study carrying an explicit UNITS field alongside SQFEET, YEARBLT, LAND_USE and sale price - it is the best schema available for a multifamily app. AUSTIN is a deliberate exclusion at rank 6: excellent parcel data in Williamson, huge market, but only 2,000 verified announced direct jobs and the most over-supplied multifamily market in the country at 23,056 permits in twelve months. Project coordinates are approximate. Where a press release stated no jobs number (Woodside Louisiana LNG) the jobs field is null rather than estimated, and where a release explicitly created zero new jobs (Graham Packaging, Hammond) the field is 0 with the retained-jobs figure in the status text.

Two of the five recommended parcel endpoints are NOT published by the parish assessor: the Lafayette layer is hosted by Es2 (es2-inc), the assessor's GIS vendor, and the Caddo layer is a Regrid/Loveland extract republished by a private economic-development ArcGIS Online account. Both were open and queryable without a token on 2026-09-04, but neither carries a service-level agreement and either could disappear. The Bossier, Tangipahoa, Lincoln and Calcasieu endpoints are all on official parish domains.

The two-letter Louisiana assessor class codes (RI, RV, CM, CI, AI, EX, RM ...) appear in BOTH the Lincoln Parish assessor layer and the Caddo Regrid extract, so they are a statewide convention rather than a local one. I could not find a published key for them anywhere and have not guessed at their meanings. If you can obtain that key from the Louisiana Tax Commission or an assessor's office, Lincoln Parish immediately becomes a much stronger candidate and Caddo's usecode field becomes usable alongside its zoning.

Louisiana is NOT a mandatory sale-price disclosure state in the way Arizona is, but sale price is nevertheless populated in the Lafayette (saleprice/saledate), Caddo (saleprice/saledate) and Tangipahoa (purchase_price/transfer_date, with a Verified flag) layers. It is absent from Bossier, Lincoln and Calcasieu.

Confirmed but rejected as a data source: https://gissrv1.romlc.net/arcgis/rest/services/WebMaps/LA_Assessors/MapServer, which is indexed on ArcGIS Online as the parcel source for Caddo, Bossier, Tangipahoa, Natchitoches and other parishes, returns error 499 'Token Required' and is unusable without credentials.

Campus proximity is scored from a published-enrollment table that now carries 118 institutions across every corridor in this catalogue — 1.2 million students — each with the term its figure refers to and a source URL. Community colleges are weighted down, health-science campuses partially. Where a figure covers more than one campus or includes online enrolment, the row says so; a wrong denominator would silently corrupt a student-housing score. One institution, Purdue University in Indianapolis, carries a null enrolment because no campus-level figure has been published since the 2024 IUPUI split.

Four project figures in this set are known not to match their announcements and are recorded that way: Apple's $1bn Research Triangle campus, promised in 2021 with 3,000 jobs, has never broken ground and North Carolina reset its milestones in November 2025 to require only 126 people by end-2027; Maxeon's $1bn Albuquerque plant was CANCELLED, its lease abandoned in February 2026; Intel promised 700 jobs at Rio Rancho and described delivery as 'hundreds'; and Novo Nordisk's Clayton expansion was followed by layoffs at that same plant. Counting Apple's 3,000 would move Raleigh from fourth to first on the jobs-per-permit ranking, and counting Maxeon would move Albuquerque from fourth to second. Neither is counted.

Youngstown-Warren ranks first on announced jobs per permit by a factor of eight, and all three of its projects - Stargate Lordstown, Foxconn/SoftBank and Ultium - sit in TRUMBULL county, whose entire GIS domain was unreachable. The records held for this metro are Mahoning county, where none of the capital is.

Four Louisiana college markets (Monroe, Thibodaux, Natchitoches, Alexandria) were researched in September 2026 and are carried as STUDIED, not live: they appear in the corridor tables with their verified enrolment, capital and permit figures, but they hold no parcels on the map. Only Monroe has a free machine-readable parcel endpoint whose schema can separate multifamily from single-family against a PUBLISHED zoning key (the City of Monroe Developer_Parcels layer, ZONING_CODE on 25,920 parcels, meanings from the city Zoning layer). Thibodaux has two working 56,000-feature layers with assessed value on 90% of rows but NO use, class or zoning field of any kind, so no property in it could be classified without guessing a use - which this platform does not do. Natchitoches and Alexandria were not recommended. Carrying the finding is the point: it records why they cannot be pulled, so the work is not repeated.
